cohort: Singleton infants without congenital anomalies born to parturient women residing in rural British Columbia between April 1, 2003, and March 31, 2008
finding: Midwives provided safe maternity care to rural parturient women, offering choice of birth place, with lower intervention rates in communities with limited obstetric services, but higher perinatal mortality among women living furthest from hospitals.
mod_finding: Rates of planned home birth were higher in most rural areas with midwife involvement, while actual home birth rates were lowest for women living furthest from hospitals.
